At last night's Emmy Awards ceremony, Apple TV+ had an outstanding performance, beating competitors like HBO to become the most-awarded platform of the night. Below is HBO's Casey Bloys' response to Apple TV+'s wins.

HBO's CEO praised Apple TV+'s excellent performance while also acknowledging that competing against a company worth a trillion dollars is 'quite challenging.'

Apple TV+ has long been compared to HBO, as both prioritize quality over quantity. Apple has even occasionally been referred to as the 'new HBO.'

Last night's Emmys further cemented this notion, as Apple TV+ surpassed HBO, Netflix, and other platforms to become the most-awarded platform of the night.

Apple TV+ swept a total of 29 awards, earning the distinction of being named the 'most-awarded network of the year,' with shows like 'Widow's Bay' standing out in particular. HBO followed closely behind with 21 awards.

Following the Emmy ceremony, HBO executive Casey Bloys was interviewed by Deadline and asked for his thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance. Here's what he had to say:

DEADLINE: What are your thoughts on Apple TV+'s performance this time around? They became the most-awarded platform at the Emmys for the first time—do you have anything to say about that? BLOYS: I'm actually really happy, because I think they're strong competitors—Zack and Jamie. We've always had strong competitors—Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon—so having Apple join the fray keeps everyone on their toes, and that's exactly the state in which I perform at my best. They're a company worth a trillion dollars, so it's undoubtedly a big challenge, but we'll keep doing what we've always done, which is making the best shows possible.

Bloys joined HBO in 2004 and has been in charge of programming since 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple TV+'s win was largely gracious and sincere, offering heartfelt congratulations.

However, the most interesting part of his response was this line: 'They're a company worth a trillion dollars, so it's undoubtedly a big challenge.'

We don't know Apple TV+'s internal budget, but there's no denying that Apple's overall financial resources far exceed those of most competitors, including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently actively seeking to acquire HBO (along with other Warner Bros. Discovery assets), hoping to compete more effectively with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does scale naturally bring advantages? Perhaps it does. But many networks have already proven that when it comes to producing content that audiences love, money is only a small part of the equation.

Apple TV+ costs $14.99 per month, and can also be purchased as part of the Apple One subscription bundle.
